title: Split Message Based on Limit
statement:
Cut the string `message` into one or more consecutive pieces and append a tag `<a/b>` to each piece, where `b` is the total number of pieces and `a` is the piece's position, counted from 1 to `b`.

- Every tagged piece except the last must be exactly `limit` characters long, tag included; the last tagged piece may be at most `limit` characters long.
- Stripping the tags and joining the pieces in order must give back `message` exactly.
- Among all splits that follow these rules, use the fewest pieces.

Return the tagged pieces in order. If no split follows the rules, return an empty array.
constraints: message contains only lowercase English letters and spaces

notes:
## Intuition

Fix the number of pieces `parts` and the split is forced: piece `a` carries `limit - len("<a/parts>")` message characters, and only the last may carry fewer. So enumerate `parts = 1, 2, 3, ...` and stop at the first count whose pieces can hold the whole message.

That room is `parts * (limit - 3 - digits(parts))` minus the digits of every index `1..parts`, which `indexDigits` accumulates, so each count is tested in O(1). The room does not grow steadily: going from 9 to 10 pieces lengthens every tag.

## Approach

1. Move `parts` from 1 up to `n` (more pieces than characters never helps), adding `digits(parts)` to `indexDigits`.
2. The last tag `<parts/parts>` has `3 + 2 * digits(parts)` characters. If that already fills `limit`, the last piece has no room, now or for any larger count, so return `[]`.
3. Compute `capacity`; if it is below `n`, try the next count.
4. Otherwise build the pieces: each takes `take = limit - suffix.length` characters from `start` (the last one just takes what is left) and gets its `suffix`.

## Example 1, step by step

`n = 37`, `limit = 9`. With 9 pieces every tag, such as `<1/9>`, has 5 characters, so each piece carries 4 and `capacity = 9 * (9 - 3 - 1) - 9 = 36`, one short. At `parts = 10` every tag grows to at least 6 characters and `capacity` falls to `10 * (9 - 3 - 2) - 11 = 29`. It first reaches 37 at `parts = 14`: `14 * 4 - 19 = 37`. Pieces 1 to 9 (tags like `<1/14>`) take 3 characters and pieces 10 to 14 take 2, giving `"thi<1/14>"` up to `"ge<14/14>"`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n): at most `n` counts are tried in O(1) each (digit counts are tiny), and building the answer copies the message once.
- Space: O(n) for the output; O(1) besides.

## Pitfalls

- Binary searching over all counts fails, because `capacity` drops whenever the digit count of `parts` grows.
- The tag `<a/b>` costs `3 + digits(a) + digits(b)` characters; forgetting the three symbols, or charging `digits(parts)` for every index, gives the wrong room.
- The last piece may be shorter than `limit`; do not pad it.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `n` | length of `message` |
| `parts` | piece count being tried |
| `indexDigits` | total digits of the indices `1..parts` |
| `capacity` | message characters that `parts` pieces can carry |
| `start` | where the next piece begins in `message` |
| `suffix`, `take` | the current piece's tag and how many characters it carries |

narration.6: Index parts is new, so add its digits.
narration.7: The longest tag, <parts/parts>, leaves no room for even one character...
narration.8: ...and tags only grow with more pieces, so no split exists.
narration.10: Characters all pieces can carry: limit minus the '<', '/', '>' and the digits of parts, per piece, minus every index's digits.
narration.11: Not enough room for the whole message with this many pieces.
narration.16: Build the forced split, piece by piece.
narration.18: A full piece carries whatever limit leaves after its tag.
narration.19: Cut the next characters (the last piece just gets the remainder) and append the tag.
narration.20: The next piece starts where this one ended.
narration.22: The first count that fits is the answer.
